svg.title: The 1979 Egypt–Israel Treaty, Sinai Return and Arab League Boycott (1978–1982)
svg.desc: Pearson Edexcel GCSE History Option P5 geopolitical map showing the 26 March 1979 Egypt–Israel Peace Treaty, phased Israeli return of the Sinai Peninsula by April 1982, annual US aid to Egypt, the November 1978 and March 1979 Baghdad Summits suspending Egypt from the Arab League, relocation of Arab League headquarters from Cairo to Tunis, diplomatic and economic boycotts by 17+ Arab states, and the 6 October 1981 assassination of Anwar Sadat in Cairo.

g.text: EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY • OPTION P5: SEPARATE PEACE & REGIONAL BACKLASH (1978–82)
The 1979 Egypt–Israel Treaty, Sinai Return & Arab League Boycott
GEOPOLITICAL ISOLATION OF EGYPT ACROSS THE ARAB WORLD (1978–1982)
Arab League HQ Moved: Cairo → Tunis (1979)
in Suez Canal & Straits of Tiran.
Killed at annual 1973 victory parade by
by Egypt's separate peace with Israel.
Signed by Sadat & Begin (witnessed by Carter);
Israel returned all Sinai & oil fields by Apr 1982
Annual US economic & military aid to Egypt.
PLO & Arab states accused Sadat of trading
Palestinian statehood simply to regain Sinai.
Cut embassies, Gulf subsidies & Arab trade.
Radical Islamists denounced peace with Israel
and mass arrests of critics as betrayal of Islam.
Egyptian Islamic Jihad soldiers shot Sadat
dead while reviewing the 1973 victory parade.
Successor Hosni Mubarak kept the treaty intact
and rejoined the Arab League in 1989.
EDEXCEL EXAM TAKEAWAY · WHY 1979 RESHAPED MIDDLE EAST CONFLICT
Removing Egypt—the strongest Arab military power—ended multi-front interstate wars against
Israel, yet isolated Cairo for a decade and shifted the conflict onto Lebanon and Palestinian rule.
